themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing you are measuring often changes while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization answers call the output non-deterministic with no fixed baseline, incrementality answers describe platforms that adapt to the holdout, and identity resolution answers say accuracy can only be checked for the small logged-in minority.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the people holding the answer gain nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blockers are money and politics, inside the company as much as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay rather than write another rule.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers propose a fast lane with real perks because agents profit by looking human, journey orchestration answers say channel owners are paid on their own numbers, and semantic context answers call conflicting definitions a political settlement, not a modeling gap.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution answers all put a proxy or gateway in front of every write with hard spend and audience caps, and consent enforcement answers route every data exit through a single checkpoint teams actually own.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch from outside and guess whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Today's consent and deletion answers agree that third-party platforms are closed boxes and that a model cannot unlearn a person without retraining, while ad supply integrity answers say the parties counting the impressions profit from not proving them.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning and context: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, whether two teams can both be right about what a word means. No rule set captures that, so the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box instead of removing it.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance answers build an approved-claims library and limit what the model may say because implied meaning cannot be checked automatically, and semantic context answers say legitimate conflicting definitions must be disclosed rather than merged.
